summary: Sprint FinTech (Stripe Connect + Escrow + Subscriptions + Admin) backend-only testing complete. 28/28 new pytest tests pass in /app/backend/tests/test_fintech_sprint.py covering ALL 22 items from the review request. Full regression green: 50/50 (test_my_home.py 27/27 + test_trust_engine.py 23/23). Grand total: 78/78 backend tests passing. No frontend testing performed (per request: backend only). MOCK_MODE confirmed active via deterministic ID prefixes (acct_mock_, pay_mock_, tr_mock_, re_mock_, sub_mock_ all observed). Commission precedence chain verified end-to-end via real escrow releases: global 1500 bps -> promo 500 bps -> exemption 0 bps (floored at 200 min_cents). Admin gating strict: /admin/* returns 403 for non-admin (pro.test) and 200 for client.test@auxora.fr (in ADMIN_EMAILS). Webhook idempotency confirmed with duplicate=true on second POST of same event_id. State machine transitions verified: pending -> held (mock-confirm) -> released/refunded/frozen; only held is releasable; only held is freezable; frozen refundable. Matching non-bias verified statically: /app/backend/services/matching.py has ZERO occurrences of 'subscription' or 'is_subscribed'.

minor.issue: Commission with bps=0 (exemption) still charges the min_cents floor (200 = 2€), because commission_amount() enforces `max(calc, min_cents)`. If truly-free exemptions are ever needed, either lower min_cents to 0 for exemption rules or bypass floor when bps==0. Current design intentional per DEFAULT_COMMISSION_MIN_CENTS=200; documenting for product.
For payment_intent.succeeded, uses `async for` inside `$in` list-comprehension to fetch payment_ids. Works but a two-step await (list first, then update_many) would be cleaner. Not blocking.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 2242 lines — STRONGLY recommend extracting fintech routers (connect_router.py, payments_router.py, escrow_router.py, subscriptions_router.py, admin_router.py) before adding installments/BNPL. Same recommendation as iteration_8.

services/payments.py (~340 lines) is a clean, self-contained wrapper — MOCK_MODE branch on every Stripe call, deterministic _mock_id() prefixes, resolve_commission_bps() precedence documented in docstring. Excellent module.

Commission precedence in resolve_commission_bps() correctly orders: exemption (artisan-specific) > active promo (lowest bps wins via sort) > trade-specific > platform_config global > DEFAULT (1000). Verified via real release flow.
Webhook idempotency correctly uses stripe_events collection with event_id key. Duplicate events return {received:true, duplicate:true} without side effects. Verified.

MOCK_MODE detection at services/payments.py:50 catches empty string, 'sk_test_emergent', and 'sk_test_placeholder' — safe fallback. When a real key is set, ONLY that line switches behavior; zero code changes needed elsewhere.
Admin gating via require_admin() uses BOTH role=='admin' OR email in ADMIN_EMAILS env allow-list — resilient. client.test@auxora.fr correctly gated as admin for tests.
matching.py verified NOT to reference subscription tiers — grep for 'subscription' and 'is_subscribed' returns zero results. Ranking invariant preserved.
State machine transitions (pending -> held -> released|refunded|frozen; frozen -> refunded) enforced by explicit 400 responses on invalid state. Good defensive coding.
Subscriptions public catalog correctly strips stripe_price_id via dict comprehension at server.py:1612 — no price ID leak. Verified.
Audit logs written on every state transition (connect create, payment intent, mock confirm, release, refund, freeze, subscription events, commission rule changes) — compliance-ready.
